products.name: Braintrust
products.note: Evaluation-first LLM platform; datasets, scorers, CI quality gates, prompt iteration with production trace feedback

reading.body:
Braintrust is an evaluation and observability platform for AI agents that catches performance regressions in production through continuous testing and automated scoring, positioning quality assurance as central to safe deployment at scale.

The core insight is that AI systems degrade silently. Without continuous evaluation, drift and regression reach users undetected. Braintrust's architecture addresses this by ingesting production traces, running evaluations against datasets and scorers, and feeding results back into prompt and dataset iteration. This is a governance problem disguised as an infrastructure one. As AI workloads move toward production and agents operate without human-in-the-loop review, the ability to measure degradation and enforce quality gates becomes a binding constraint on scale.

The platform's emphasis on CI-style quality gates reflects a maturation in how teams think about AI reliability. Traditional software testing catches logical errors. Braintrust catches behavioral drift, which is categorically different and harder to define. The use of automated scoring and the Loop feature suggest the company is betting that quality feedback can be systematized at the speed production now demands.

The data does not indicate Braintrust's compute consumption, power footprint, or infrastructure needs. It does not reveal adoption across the market, deployment patterns, or whether its evaluations represent a constraint on how fast models can be retrained and redeployed. The 181 California law exposure entries suggest regulatory surface area but provide no detail on what risks drive that count.

profile_text.body:
Braintrust is a San Francisco, California company founded in 2022. Its site describes it as an AI observability platform for tracing production, running evals, and catching regressions before they reach users, with the stated aim of shipping quality agents at scale. The company says AI drifts and regresses silently, and that surfacing patterns automatically lets teams evaluate against expectations and iterate continuously.

The product tracked under the Braintrust name is described as an evaluation-first LLM platform covering datasets, scorers, CI quality gates, and prompt iteration with production trace feedback. The site also describes Loop, which generates prompts, scorers, and datasets automatically from a description of what the user wants to optimize, and an MCP server that connects a coding agent to the AI stack so logs can be queried, evals run, and prompts updated directly from an IDE.

No litigation cases are listed for the company. Its law exposure record names California with a count of 281.
